title: Guidelines for Media when Approaching Those Affected by Traumatic Event
what_it_is: Guidelines for Media when Approaching Those Affected by Traumatic Event

sections.label: Media access to school compound
sections.summary: Media were kept outside the school compound and asked not to press students or staff for identifiable interviews, photos or videos.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: When the incident took place, the media was not given access to the school compound and was restricted to public areas outside the school.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The media’s understanding was sought not to press students or staff for interviews or take photographs or videos of them in a way that they could be identified.

sections.label: AGC reminder on CYPA protections
sections.summary: The AGC reminded mainstream media that the CYPA bars publishing information identifying anyone under 18 involved in Court proceedings, including witnesses.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: In addition, the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) has also reminded the mainstream media about the legal protections accorded to those under 18, as part of the Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA).

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Under the CYPA, no one is allowed to publish or broadcast information that identifies or is calculated to identify any person below 18 years old who is involved in any Court proceedings, including as a witness.

sections.label: CYPA protection for minors
sections.summary: The CYPA protects minors under 18 involved in or witnessing a crime, and legal recourse exists against anyone publishing identifying information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The CYPA does accord protection to minors below 18 years old who may have been involved or had witnessed a crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, if any mainstream or online media, or for that matter, anyone in his or her own capacity, ends up publishing any information that identifies the minor, there is legal recourse to take that offender to task.

sections.label: Media in public areas outside school
sections.summary: Media were asked not to approach students and staff outside the school gate, but in public areas they broke no laws and authorities could do only so much.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, we had sought the mainstream media as well as the online media's efforts not to approach the students and staff outside the school gate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: However, as reporters and media crew were in public areas, they were not actually breaking any laws, and they were entitled to be there as long as they wanted since they were not breaking any public safety laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There was only so much the authorities could do to disperse them.
